sm: In a Q and A after his talk, Douglas Axe argues that a two-year-old's recognition that complex things were made is genuine science, which he calls common science as opposed to technical science. He says intuition is a loose category that includes observation and quick deduction, and that creativity works by inspired jumps rather than trying all possibilities. He clarifies he is not endorsing all intuition, only that this one has scientific validity, and he says his book also contains detailed research chapters. On bad design, he says he addresses examples like piranhas, viruses and cancer without fully solving them. On Thomas Nagel, he says Nagel would agree that accidents cannot explain humans and that mind and purpose are real, but Nagel wants nature without God, while Axe argues for a personal God.
